Phase 1 implementation commenced in May 2024 with construction of the Autonomous Innovation Center (AIC) operations and maintenance facility, which houses the state-of-the-art operations control center for all AV fleets in service within the U2C district. This facility opened in April 2025 while the Phase 1 fleet AVs were being tested along the Bay Street Innovation Corridor ahead of the June launch. The AV service is called NAVI, or Neighborhood Autonomous Vehicle Innovation. The U2C Phase 1 route (shown in blue in Figure 15) is 3.5 miles in round-trip length, connecting downtown Jacksonville with the sports complex (far right). Twelve stations will be served by 14 vehicles in operation. Source: JTA The NAVI service initially uses 14 Ford E-Transit battery electric passenger models. These vehicles are compliant with Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards and ADA. The vehicles are equipped with an ADS provided by Oxa (formerly Oxbotica of Cambridge, England).1 During early operations, a safety attendant will be on board each vehicle at all times. To accommodate the project requirements for the all-electric AV fleet, provisions for battery charging are a key aspect of the AIC facility design. There are 14 Level 2 charging stations and two Level 3 DC fast charge stations at the facility to support NAVI’s daily operations. The AIC also includes a solar panel array, a microgrid power supply capable of providing a significant portion of the total energy needs within the facility (though not for vehicle charging). Figure 16 shows the NAVI vehicles and the AIC facility where the vehicle fleet will be operated, with light maintenance performed and battery charging infrastructure also provided at the AIC.
